title: Hurwitz zeta as polygamma master: zeta(n+1, a) = (-1)^{n+1} psi^{(n)}(a) / n!
latent_structure: One meromorphic master (Hurwitz zeta in the a-plane, or equivalently polygamma) generates the whole tower of thermal pole sums of order n+1. The identity is the special-value bridge 25.11.12, not the trigamma series 5.15.1 (which is the n=1 expansion of the same master). Reconstruction: scale by n! and a sign.

function_domains.zeta: Hurwitz zeta zeta(s,a): series for Re s>1 and a != 0,-1,-2,... (DLMF 25.11.1); meromorphic continuation in s with only a simple pole at s=1; analytic in Re a>0 at fixed s != 1
function_domains.polygamma: psi^{(n)} meromorphic; poles of order n+1 at nonpositive integers (DLMF 5.15)

analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: DLMF 25.11.12 lives in 25.11(v) with the written half-plane

analytic_domains.statement: a is not a nonpositive integer

analytic_domains.label: DERIVED

branch_conventions: principal factorial n! for positive integers; no extra branch of zeta(s,a) on Re a>0, s=n+1>=2

why_not_cse_lgg: Hurwitz zeta and polygamma are different named heads. CSE cannot identify zeta(n+1,a) with a scaled psi^{(n)}(a). The latent is a single master with an n-family of reconstructions, not a local rewrite.
proposer_leak_risk: Source names zeta and psi^{(n)}. Do not leak 'Hurwitz master', 'thermal pole tower', or 'same as 5.15.1' in proposer context. Keep the two-head residual only.
notes: zeta and polygamma are both special functions; n=1 is psi'(a)=zeta(2,a), which is equivalent to summing 5.15.1 only after using 25.11.1. The packaged identity here is the master bridge with Re a>0 written, not the trigamma series. Distinct from thermal-05 and thermal-06.
